title: How Much Does Quattr Cost? What Is Public, and Who It Fits
metaTitle: How Much Does Quattr Cost? Quote-Only Pricing Explained
metaDescription: Quattr publishes no prices: it is a demo-gated, custom quote as of October 2026. See what is verifiable, what drives cost, and if it fits a small business.
shortAnswer: Quattr does not publish a price. As of 3 October 2026, its pricing page is a “Book a Demo” form, its own comparison page says “Custom pricing,” and Capterra and GetApp list no number, so any dollar figure for Quattr is unverified. Treat it as a quote-based purchase for teams with a search budget. Most small businesses should get a free AI visibility baseline first and book the demo only if a specific job needs Quattr’s execution tools.
intro:
This guide is based on Quattr’s public pages and third-party listings as of October 2026. We have not tested Quattr hands-on and have no quote from its sales team, so we state only what those pages say.

An earlier version of this page repeated tier prices ($79, $249 and $599 a month) from review aggregators. We found no current, checkable source for them, so we removed them.

sections.heading: How much does Quattr cost?
sections.body:
Quattr’s price is custom and quote-only. There are no public tiers, no monthly figure and no self-serve checkout, and that is what Quattr, Capterra and GetApp each show as of 3 October 2026.

What you can verify yourself:

- **Quattr’s [pricing page](https://www.quattr.com/pricing)** lists no price or plan. It is a form headed “Personalized to your site. 30 seconds to book,” with three ticks: “No credit card,” “30-min call” and “Free trial included.”
- **Quattr’s [comparison page](https://www.quattr.com/compare/quattr-vs-profound)** describes its pricing as “Custom pricing (based on your use cases; just pay for features you actually use).”
- **[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/253750/Quattr/)** says “Contact vendor for pricing” and shows a free trial.
- **[GetApp](https://www.getapp.com/all-software/a/quattr/)** shows “No pricing info” beside “Starting from.”
- **The trial route** depends on your use case: Quattr’s FAQ lists a demo, sandbox, free trial, proof of concept or paid pilot.

One trap: on that comparison page, “Starts at $99/month for SMBs” sits in the Profound column, not Quattr’s. It is Quattr’s claim about a competitor, and we have not checked it against Profound’s own site. It is easy to misread as Quattr’s entry price.

Look-alike names (Quartr, Quartile, Quattro) show up in price searches with their own numbers. Check the domain is quattr.com.

sections.heading: What is Quattr, exactly?
sections.body:
Quattr is an AI search growth platform that tracks your brand in AI answers and Google, then prepares the content, links and fixes to improve it. Its [homepage](https://www.quattr.com/) names ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and AI Overviews, and says you control what goes live.

It covers SEO, answer engine optimization (AEO) and [generative engine optimization (GEO)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_engine_optimization), the practice of improving visibility in AI-generated answers. The public pages describe:

- **Tracking:** citations, mentions, sentiment and competitor presence across those engines.
- **An agent called GIGA** that prepares page refreshes, new pages and fixes for your review.
- **Internal linking** that is reversible and sampled before rollout, plus pages that arrive as CMS drafts. The comparison page lists WordPress as the native publishing integration “now.”
- **First-party data:** Search Console and GA4 joins, so citations can be tied to sessions and conversions.
- **People:** “Every customer works with a Quattr Strategist.”

Its proof points are its own: 4.9/5 from 65 G2 reviews, and named results from Kiteworks (+79% AI Overview presence) and CloudEagle (3x AI citation share). A March 2026 [press release](https://www.quattr.com/press-release/g2-spring-report-2026) calls the company a platform for “mid-market and enterprise brands.”

![Three colleagues reviewing charts and plans together at a shared desk in a modern office](https://images.pexels.com/photos/8278898/pexels-photo-8278898.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

**What we saw on quattr.com itself.** In [AEOeye’s crawler access study](/resources/ai-crawler-access-study-2026-10.csv) (3 October 2026), Quattr’s robots.txt blocks no AI bots, it serves no llms.txt (a 404), and its homepage HTML carries Organization and WebSite JSON-LD only. That describes its website, not the product.

sections.heading: What drives Quattr’s price?
sections.body:
Quattr says price follows your use cases, so the drivers are the modules and scale you switch on. It does not publish which ones move the quote, so read this list as questions for the sales call, not as a rate card.

What Quattr’s own pages name:

- **Execution modules:** Optimize Pages, Create & Publish Pages, Internal Linking AI and the Landing Page Generator.
- **Scale:** multi-domain management, large keyword sets and governance, per its FAQ.
- **Human help:** a Strategist for every customer, and a “Growth Concierge” for enterprise-scale teams.

Opaque pricing is not a red flag, since enterprise tools scope by site. It is a fit signal: the vendor expects a buyer with a budget line.

Ask these five things before you book:

1. Which modules are in my quote, and which are optional?
2. Do I pay per domain, prompt, page, seat or a flat fee?
3. What does the trial include, and who approves it?
4. What is the minimum term, and what happens at renewal?
5. What must I supply (data access, CMS access, staff time) before the first result?

sections.heading: Is Quattr a good fit for a small business?
sections.body:
Usually not as a first purchase. Quattr positions itself for mid-market and enterprise teams, and most of its value is execution at a scale a small site cannot yet use. It can fit a small business that already runs a real SEO program and has a platform budget.

The public evidence points both ways:

- **Against:** the March 2026 [press release](https://www.quattr.com/press-release/g2-spring-report-2026) says it is built for “mid-market and enterprise brands,” and entry is a sales call.
- **For:** [Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/253750/Quattr/) lists “Freelancers, Small businesses, Mid size businesses, Enterprises” as typical users. The demo form has a “1-50 employees” option. The press release also says G2 rated it a High Performer in Content Creation across Enterprise, Mid-Market and Small-Business segments.

Small companies are welcome. The question is whether you can use what you would pay for.

![Young professionals discussing work around a table in a bright startup workspace](https://images.pexels.com/photos/39190475/pexels-photo-39190475.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

Our position is that most small businesses have a presence problem, not a tracking problem. In [AEOeye’s recommendation benchmark](/resources/aeoeye-recommendation-benchmark-2026-09.json) (127 audits, 27 brand names, 892 answers, June to September 2026), a brand was named in 17.6% of answers. That sample is small and self-selected, so it is not an industry average, but it shows the shape of the problem: in most answers the brand is simply absent.

A tracker measures that gap; it does not close it. Execution tools can, but only with enough pages for internal linking and testing to matter.

We could not read G2 review text (G2 blocks automated fetches), so we do not quote reviewers on setup. From Quattr’s own pages we infer real work: connecting Search Console, GA4 and a CMS, then reviewing prepared changes. Plan on hours from someone who owns SEO.

**Quattr fits you if all of these are true:**

- Someone owns SEO and will use the platform weekly.
- Your site is large enough that hand-built internal linking and refreshes are a chore.
- Your CMS is WordPress, the one native integration its comparison page names.
- You have already confirmed an AI visibility gap.

**Skip it for now if** you do not know whether AI engines name you, you run marketing alone, or you need a price before any call.

sections.heading: What are cheaper ways to start?
sections.body:
Start with a free baseline, fix what it shows, and add paid tooling only when a specific job demands it. Each step below costs less than a demo cycle and shows whether you need Quattr at all.

1. **Run the free audit ($0).** [AEOeye’s free audit](/) asks ChatGPT three unbranded buyer questions live and shows the full answers, the competitors it recommends instead, and starter fixes.
2. **Check other engines by hand.** Our [free AI visibility checker guide](/blog/free-ai-visibility-checker) shows how.
3. **Fix the fundamentals.** Google says there are [“no additional requirements”](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) for AI Overviews or AI Mode and no special markup to add, and that AI-feature traffic is counted in Search Console. Quattr’s own [free AI SEO tools](https://www.quattr.com/ai-seo-tools) (title, H1, URL and meta description generators) cover on-page basics.
4. **Buy the one-time report ($29).** It adds Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity, ten questions instead of three, and a full fix roadmap. There is no subscription.
5. **Add monitoring only if you need it.** [Otterly’s Lite plan](https://otterly.ai/pricing) lists $29 a month (monthly billing, checked 3 October 2026) for 15 prompts across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot, with Claude, Gemini and AI Mode as paid add-ons.

AEOeye is not a daily tracker and does not write your content. For the wider field, see [best AI visibility tools](/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools), [Quattr alternatives](/alternatives/quattr) and [AEOeye vs Quattr](/vs/quattr).

![Three professionals working on laptops and documents in a stylish office](https://images.pexels.com/photos/7654133/pexels-photo-7654133.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=1200)

Book the demo when you have a baseline, an owner, and a job of execution volume (refreshing and linking hundreds of pages) rather than measurement.

keyTakeaways: Quattr publishes no price: its pricing page is a demo form, and Capterra and GetApp show none (checked 3 October 2026).
Ignore circulating figures of $79, $249, $599 or $99 a month. We could not verify them, and the $99 on Quattr’s own page sits in Profound’s column.
Price follows your use cases, so ask which modules, scale unit and minimum term your quote assumes.
Quattr suits teams with an SEO owner, a large WordPress site and a confirmed gap; most small businesses should start free.

faqs.a: No. As of 3 October 2026, Quattr’s pricing page shows only a demo request form, and its comparison page calls its pricing “Custom.” Capterra says “Contact vendor for pricing,” and GetApp shows “No pricing info.” To get a number you need a quote from Quattr’s team.

faqs.q: Is $99 a month the price of Quattr?
faqs.a: We could not verify that. The only “$99/month for SMBs” we found on quattr.com sits in the Profound column of Quattr’s own Quattr-versus-Profound comparison table. It is Quattr’s claim about Profound, and we did not check it against Profound’s site. It is not a Quattr list price.

faqs.q: Does Quattr have a free trial?
faqs.a: Quattr’s demo page ticks “Free trial included” and “No credit card,” and Capterra shows a free trial. Quattr’s FAQ says the offer depends on your use case and buying process, from a demo or sandbox to a proof of concept or paid pilot. Ask what your trial includes and who approves it.

faqs.q: Is Quattr good for a small business?
faqs.a: Rarely as a first purchase. Quattr describes itself as built for mid-market and enterprise brands, and its value is execution at scale. A small business with an SEO owner, a large WordPress site and budget can fit. Otherwise, run a free baseline first and book a demo only for a specific execution job.

faqs.q: What is a cheaper way to check my AI visibility than booking a demo?
faqs.a: Run AEOeye’s free audit, which asks ChatGPT three buyer questions and shows the full answers and the competitors named instead. Add the $29 one-time report for Claude, Gemini, Google AI and Perplexity. For ongoing monitoring, trackers with public prices, such as Otterly’s $29 monthly Lite plan, exist.
